chunks: Do not be quick in exposing anyone’s sin for he may be forgiven for it, and do not feel yourself safe even for a small sin because you may be punished for it

Therefore, every one of you who comes to know the faults of others should not expose them in view of what he knows about his own faults, and he should remain busy in thanks that he has been saved from what others have been indulging in
ai.seo_question: How should a Muslim behave when observing the sins of others?
ai.summary: In this passage from *Nahj al-Balagha*, Imam Ali (AS) establishes a dialectic between divine mercy for the sinner and the hidden spiritual vulnerability of the critic, urging believers to replace judgment with gratitude (*shukr*). This teaching underscores the Shia emphasis on *hilm* (forbearance) and self-reflection (*muhasaba*), warning that one’s own minor sins may outweigh their observation of another’s fault. It serves as a practical guide for maintaining social harmony and spiritual humility in the face of human imperfection.
